chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'When shall I pray Dhuhr?' He said: 'Pray eight (rak'at) at zawaal, then pray Dhuhr, then pray your optional prayer (subha), whether long or short, then pray Asr.'

key_terms.الزَّوَال: Zawaal — the moment when the sun begins its decline from its zenith, marking the onset of Dhuhr prayer time
key_terms.ثَمَانِيَةً: Eight rak'at — the supererogatory nawafil prayers before Dhuhr in the Shia tradition
key_terms.سُبْحَة: Subha — optional/supererogatory prayer; here refers to the nawafil between Dhuhr and Asr

ai.seo_question: When should Dhuhr prayer be prayed according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: A companion, Darih al-Muharbi, asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the proper timing for the midday (Dhuhr) prayer. The Imam prescribes a specific sequence: eight supererogatory rak'at at zawaal (the moment the sun begins to decline from its zenith), followed by the obligatory Dhuhr, then the optional subha prayers of any length, and finally the obligatory Asr. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential tradition of recommending supererogatory nawafil prayers before and between the obligatory daily prayers, particularly the eight rak'at that mark the beginning of the midday devotional period.
